column1: Geometry Gains — per-satellite gain, actual errors, stealth window and dropped reports (manuscript supplementary material, v2.0)

Assumed Walker-Star variants, 200 satellites, 500 km, inclination 86 deg, aircraft at 10 km; 12,960 samples per variant (19 latitudes x 8 longitudes x 90 epochs). e_h = g_i*eps; HDOP^2 = sum g_i^2; h* = 350/30 = 11.7 is a necessary-condition screening threshold. Residual test: T = sigma*sqrt(chi2_(n-3)(1-P_FA)), P_FA = 1e-3; sigma 10/30/100 m is illustrative (the monitor of the reference design is not published). The 350 m statistic (RMS, percentile, maximum) is to be confirmed against the standard. Scripts: geometry/hdop*.py, gain*.py; seeds 1 and 7.
B. Share of samples with an open stealth window (k = factor by which the threshold is raised; k=2, 4 model the enabler T3.06)
C. Reports dropped (T2.04): 10x20, 0 deg; worst of 400 random subsets per sample; 1,200 samples

column7: Share with 30 m step breaching 350 m

column2: Gain of the best-placed satellite is about half the HDOP in the median sample (ratio 0.47-0.55); in the tail the two coincide. A 30 m step breaches 350 m only where g_max >= 11.7 and in all of those samples it stays below the residual-test detection level. Monte-Carlo check of the linear model: simulated rms error agrees with sigma*HDOP within 2.3 %.
